newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Five killed in Colombia cement plant disaster.
newsitem.headline: Five killed in Colombia cement plant disaster.

text.p: At least five people were killed and a dozen others were seriously injured on Friday when red-hot material used to manufacture cement rained down on workers in a factory in central Colombia, authorities said.
Alvaro Ramirez, mayor of the city of Ibague in Tolima province, said the accident at the Caracolito cement plant on the city's outskirts occurred at about 1:35 p.m.
Spokesmen for Cementos Diamante, owner of the plant, could not be reached for immediate comment and failed to return several calls to their Bogota offices.

But Fire Department officials said the accident apparently occurred when workers sought to clear a blockage in one of the pre-heaters that a mix of sand, limestone, coal and other raw materials pass through before being poured into a large kilm where they are blended at extremely high temperatures into cement.
The accident caused fiery hot raw material to fly through the factory like napalm, burning almost everything in its path, witnesses said.
Perry Winfield, chief cement analyst at Paribas in New York, described the three-year-old Ibague plant as "state-of-the-art" and said it accounted for about one-third of the output of Diamante.

Winfield quoted sources at Mexican cement giant Cementos Mexicanos, the owner of Diamante, as saying the blockage in one of five pre-heaters at the Ibague plant caused it to shut down on Thursday and that workers were attempting to clear it manually when the accident occurred.

Guillermo Linares, head of medical services at the local Social Security Institute hospital in Ibague, initially said four workers were killed in the blast and that 16 others were being treated for burns.
But Ricardo Rivas, another medical director at the hospital, later told reporters the number of fatalities had increased to five and that no more than 12 burn victims remained under treatment.
